name: intraday-equities-jpm-h20
notes: JPM-only horizon probe, H in {5,10,15,20}. DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A LOCK. Four differences from run-hstar-cv-postcovid.json. (1) One name: JPM has no split in the post-COVID window, so the unadjusted-split blocker (unadjusted-stock-splits-in-the-raw-alpaca-tape.md) cannot contaminate this run; AAPL is dropped for exactly that reason. (2) The horizon grid stops at 20 minutes, so the Newey-West correction inside no_information_test needs at most 3 lags on a ~3.3k-row window instead of the 233 the 1170 grid demanded. A week-block bootstrap buys nothing at this bandwidth; it is the fix for long horizons, not short ones. (3) features.lookback=20 emits one-minute ret_lag columns for the last 20 minutes on top of the 66 session features, so the tree can see minute-scale momentum changes the 5-minute scales average away. (4) The HPO is widened from 8 draws to 32 over a space that spans underfitting (7 leaves, depth 3, 400 min_child) to overfitting (63 leaves, depth 8, 50 min_child), and scores on IC rather than MSPE. Read train_ic against val_ic per fold to place the winner between the two failure modes. LookbackScan is absent, so its all-prior training defect does not apply.

universe.notes: The H<=20 grid variant. lead_start=5 is also the training label.

alpaca.notes: Historical SIP tape, adjustment raw. Run from the child root.

session.notes: Regular session only; the store keeps every vendor minute.

momentum_horizons.notes: Few minutes; sharper than the 5m scale in the 46.
Condenses the old L=120 window into ret/rv/mom.
Few hours, still inside one RTH session.
Five RTH sessions, about a week.

features.notes: lookback=20 is the only change from the 66-feature build: it emits one-minute ret_lag columns for the last 20 minutes. Those lags carry 20 minutes of memory against scale features reaching three sessions, so expect importance to sit mostly outside them; the point is to give the tree a minute-resolution view of momentum turning. Lags never bridge a tape gap. layout=columns means the scan reads the frame's own names, so every emitted column is seen and keep_features is not consulted.

tradable.notes: SPY has already entered the residual features; score tradables.

jpm.notes: One name. Sits after tradable so the cohort that built the cross-sectional features is untouched. JPM is split-free across the sample, which is why it is the one kept.

scan.notes: No min_split_gain anywhere: gain is measured in squared-loss units and the 5-minute label variance is near 2.6e-06, so any nonzero threshold makes every tree a stump (the b5967dff failure). reg_lambda is safe to search because it enters as N/(N+lambda) against the leaf sample count, not against the label scale. hpo_objective=ic rather than the mspe default: at this signal-to-noise the flattest model wins on MSPE and a constant forecast is the MSPE optimum outright, so an MSPE search selects toward underfitting by construction. The search runs on an inner holdout carved from fold TRAIN; fold validation stays unread, so the val_ic reported per fold is not a tuned number. The node refuses a fold whose forecast is constant.

walkforward.notes: Same post-COVID folds as run-hstar-cv-postcovid.json so the two are comparable: first validation 2022-05-06, twenty 63-day steps, a real 730-day bounded training window, last validation inside the 2025-11-30 cut. objective is val_ic, NOT go_frac: counting fold-level rejections and taking the max is vote counting, which Hedges-Olkin showed is inconsistent when per-fold power is below one half (A0035). The winner here only labels a fold in the summary; the science is the per-fold sequence, which is what the block-by-block reading needs. embargo_days=5 is now larger than any label window on this grid (20 minutes), so no training row's label can reach into validation.

sinks.notes: Local sqlite beside the invoking cwd.

tracking.notes: Excluded from identity - where metrics land is not what it computes.
